- **self**: Ollama memory estimation and multi-GPU placement: SCHED_SPREAD / layer offload fit (10/5)

## Definitions

- [statement] OLLAMA_SCHED_SPREAD is a boolean env var described in source as 'Always schedule model across all GPUs', overriding the prefer-single-GPU default. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/envconfig/config.go · keywords: Ollama memory estimation and multi-GPU placement: SCHED_SPREAD / layer offload fit · also: https://knightli.com/2026/04/19/ollama-multiple-gpu-notes/

## Structure and components

- [statement] Vendor-reported benchmark: gemma3:12b at 128k context on one RTX 4090 went from 48/49 to 49/49 GPU layers and 52.02 to 85.54 tok/s; mistral-small3.2 with image input on two RTX 4090s went from 40/41 to 41/41 layers. The post gives no mechanism detail for multi-GPU gains and does not mention SCHED_SPREAD. (low confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-23) — https://ollama.com/blog/new-model-scheduling · keywords: Ollama memory estimation and multi-GPU placement: SCHED_SPREAD / layer offload fit
- [statement] Multi-GPU does not pool into one fast GPU: layers/tensors are split across devices with cross-device transfer overhead, so its main value is fitting larger models, not linear speedup; forcing a split of a model that fits one GPU can be slower. (medium confidence) — https://knightli.com/2026/04/19/ollama-multiple-gpu-notes/ · keywords: Ollama memory estimation and multi-GPU placement: SCHED_SPREAD / layer offload fit · also: https://docs.ollama.com/faq
- [statement] The num_gpu option is a count of layers to offload, not a number of GPUs. (low confidence) — https://glukhov.org/llm-performance/ollama/memory-allocation-in-ollama-new-version/ · keywords: Ollama memory estimation and multi-GPU placement: SCHED_SPREAD / layer offload fit

## Measurements and reference values

- [statement] Independent single-16GB-GPU test on v0.12.1: for models too big for VRAM, three of four (mistral-small3.2:24b, gemma3:27b, qwen3:32b) shifted slightly more to CPU (e.g. 41%->44%, 28%->29%, 30%->32% CPU); qwen3:30b-a3b unchanged. Contradicts the vendor claim; anecdotal, one machine, unnamed old version. (low confidence) — https://glukhov.org/llm-performance/ollama/memory-allocation-in-ollama-new-version/ · keywords: Ollama memory estimation and multi-GPU placement: SCHED_SPREAD / layer offload fit
- [statement] Diagnose offload with `ollama ps`: the PROCESSOR column shows 100% GPU or a CPU/GPU split; with the new scheduler the vendor says nvidia-smi figures should match ollama ps. (medium confidence) — https://knightli.com/2026/04/19/ollama-multiple-gpu-notes/ · keywords: Ollama memory estimation and multi-GPU placement: SCHED_SPREAD / layer offload fit · also: https://ollama.com/blog/new-model-scheduling

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Ollama blog (2025-09-23): the new engine measures the exact memory a model needs before running instead of estimating it; enabled by default for models on the new engine (gpt-oss, llama4, gemma3, qwen3, mistral-small3.2, embedding models and others), with more migrating. (medium confidence) (verified as of 2025-09-23) — https://ollama.com/blog/new-model-scheduling · keywords: Ollama memory estimation and multi-GPU placement: SCHED_SPREAD / layer offload fit · also: https://glukhov.org/llm-performance/ollama/memory-allocation-in-ollama-new-version/

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Default multi-GPU placement: if the model fits entirely on any single GPU, Ollama loads it on that GPU (less PCIe traffic); only if it does not fit on one GPU is it spread across all available GPUs. (high confidence) — https://docs.ollama.com/faq · keywords: Ollama memory estimation and multi-GPU placement: SCHED_SPREAD / layer offload fit · also: https://knightli.com/2026/04/19/ollama-multiple-gpu-notes/
- [statement] OLLAMA_GPU_OVERHEAD reserves a number of bytes of VRAM per GPU (default 0), shrinking what the scheduler treats as available. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/envconfig/config.go · keywords: Ollama memory estimation and multi-GPU placement: SCHED_SPREAD / layer offload fit
- [statement] Current envconfig exposes llama.cpp fit controls: LLAMA_ARG_FIT (auto-fit unset memory options, default on) and LLAMA_ARG_FIT_TARGET (free VRAM margin per device, MiB). (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-14) — https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ollama/ollama/main/envconfig/config.go · keywords: Ollama memory estimation and multi-GPU placement: SCHED_SPREAD / layer offload fit
